title: Reconstruction analysis: do outcomes depend on the iterations papers erase?
direction: Marine Denolle (PI), October 28, 2026: papers are the paper's account, not its chronology, and omit loops; reconstruct each workflow in layers (reported, review-induced, disclosed, revised) and ask what maximizes outcome
drafted: Claude Code workflow agent, October 28, 2026; the PI freezes
population: 2022 Copernicus papers with an open discussion (referee and author comments on the discussion page and a discussion preprint), drawn in round 1 by equal cnp quintiles of the corpus preselection, in round 2 from the open-access preselection (at most 4 per journal) and in cop22 by an equal quota per journal spread over impact quintiles; the advance pilot papers excluded
nature_family_exclusion: The Nature Communications and Communications Earth & Environment papers of the cop22 draw are outside this plan by design: their peer review files carry no AC or AR author units, and the review addendum codes disclosures by those units. (They would also fail C4: no discussion preprint.)

features:
Features (per paper; from the kept disclosures of the set's review coding and g31_reconstruct.paper() on the set's
inquiry and review codings, with the real coding paths hashed and no E4 labels, so every input is a defined prompt,
schema and validator task)
  outside_only_loops   distinct loop events visible only outside the paper: kept disclosures of kind tried_dropped or
                       added_for_review with final_paper_status 'absent', or with removed true (the paper no longer
                       carries it); events() below
  events()             two items are one event when they share a document (g31 DISCLOSURE MATCH document rule: AC1, AR2)
                       and g31.qcov() >= g31.DMATCH, or when g31.qcov() >= SAME_EVENT_OTHER_DOC in different documents
                       (the same reply posted twice, or an AR page repeating an AC paragraph; g30 MATCH_OTHER_UNIT)
  tried_dropped        events() over kept tried_dropped disclosures (any final status)
  review_loops         g31 measure review_loops (review steps by referee, editor or commenter, move not declined)
  review_V_loops       review_loops whose node is V
  claim_narrowed       events() over kept claim_narrowed disclosures
  revision_share       g31 paper_steps_absent_in_preprint / paper_steps_located
  paper_returns, paper_revisits, paper_steps   g31 measures of the reported walk
  disclosures, disclosures_dropped             kept and dropped disclosures
  Decomposition features: oo_tried_dropped, oo_added_for_review (outside_only_loops of one kind only). Sensitivity
  features: outside_only_loops_flagged (items with loop true only); review_added_V_in_paper (added_for_review, node V,
  final present or partly); oo_e4_g27 (round 1 only: g31's default outside_only_loops with calc1-review, E4 labels and g27
  disclosures, as in derived/reconstruct/merged_walks.json); response_words (words of the AC paragraphs of
  discussion.txt plus the AR document)
outcomes:
Outcomes (advance coding, RUBRIC.md v1.1.0; g24 derived() and check_advance.basis_gain())
  achieved   verdict achieved 1, else 0 (unassessable U1-U3, U5 stay as 0; U4 excluded), as g24 'achieved'
  achieved_assessable   achieved on assessable papers only (S7)
  score      advance_score 1-5, papers with verdict achieved or not_demonstrated
  W3         criterion W3 of the verdict-basis gain (G1 when not_demonstrated) met or not_applicable 1, not_met 0;
             assessable papers
  W_count    number of W1-W4 of that gain met (W3 not_applicable counts as met), 0-4; assessable papers
  overreach  overreach.exceeds_warrant no 0, partly 1, yes 2; assessable papers
  cnp, fwci  the set's metrics.json (secondary family)

hypotheses.theory: selection under test: a claim that survived alternatives tried and dropped, and tests run only for review, is more often warranted as reported; rival (requests follow weak papers) predicts a negative sign
as H1, on the size of the warranted gain
alternatives tried before the reported route (any final status): the reported route is the survivor
referees ask for checks of the principal threat; the checks added enter the paper the blind coder reads
work reopened at review adds warrant to the published text (uncertainty, checks, consistency)
a claim narrowed at review fits its warrant in the published text; rival (narrowing is asked of overreaching papers and stays partial) predicts a positive sign
steps written after submission are mostly answers to review and add warrant the coder can see
loops the paper reports are selected for the argument; the claim that H8 is weaker than H1 is tested separately (one-sided bootstrap of H1 minus H8, CONTRAST_ALPHA)

decomposition.D1_tried_dropped: H1, H2 with oo_tried_dropped: tried and dropped, absent from the paper (selection among routes)
decomposition.D2_added_for_review: H1, H2 with oo_added_for_review: analyses added for review and kept out of the paper; they cannot add warrant the blind coder sees, so an association here is selection or confounding (for example how conscientious the team is), not added warrant

rule:
For each hypothesis: partial Spearman within strata. Ranks of feature, outcome and covariates; feature and
           outcome ranks residualized on stratum indicators and covariate ranks (OLS); rho = correlation of the two
           residuals. Two-sided p: Freedman-Lane permutation, the outcome residual permuted within stratum and
           residualized again (NPERM); 95% interval: bootstrap of papers within stratum (NBOOT); generator g20.gen
           ('recon|<id>'). Strata: journal (DOI 10.5194/<abbr>-) x set, because the three sets were drawn by different
           designs; inside each set, journals with fewer than MIN_STRATUM papers in the hypothesis's population are
           pooled into one stratum of that set. Covariates: paper_steps, paper_returns, paper_revisits, less the feature
           itself. Testable when the outcome varies and at least MIN_N papers lie above the feature's minimum and at
           least MIN_N below its maximum; else p = 1, kept in the family.
           Benjamini-Hochberg over the primary family (H1-H8) and separately over the secondary family (S01-S14, sets in
           SECONDARY_EXCLUDE left out); supported when
           q < Q and the sign is the predicted one, reversed when q < Q and the sign is opposite, else not supported.
strata: journal x set, journals under min_stratum pooled within their set
support: H1 and H2 are the primary pair; the answer uses them alone. For the population above, and for reported warrant as the blind coder judges it: "yes, positive" when H1 or H2 is supported and neither is reversed; "yes, negative" (the rival: requests follow weak papers) when H1 or H2 is reversed and neither is supported; "inconsistent" when one is supported and the other reversed; "no association detected" otherwise, qualified "rho of 0.2 or more excluded" when the upper bound of the 95% interval of both H1 and H2 is below 0.2. S6 (round 1, agent labels) is reported beside the answer as sign concordance with H1 and H2, not as a condition.
contrast: H1 minus H8 (partial rho of outside_only_loops minus that of paper_returns against achieved, same papers and strata): "H1 stronger than H8" when the one-sided paired-bootstrap p (share of 500 resamples with a difference <= 0) is below 0.05; reported beside the family, not part of the answer.
shared_method: The review coding (disclosures, final_paper_status) and the advance coding are made by the same model family (claude-opus-5-5) from text of the same paper. The advance coder reads only the blinded published text (tools/blind_text.py) and sees no review record; the review coder reads the review record and the published paper. A shared response to how much the paper reports is possible in both directions: a terse paper makes more disclosures absent and gives less reported warrant (bias toward a negative H1), a long paper with long responses gives more disclosures and more reported warrant (bias toward a positive H1). S2 adds log paper words, log response words, log author and reference counts and disclosures_dropped. The method is not shared equally across features: H7, H8 and the covariates come from the same published text that the advance outcome is read from, by the same model family, while the H1 feature comes from the review record; H8 therefore carries more shared-method variance than H1, which biases the H1 minus H8 contrast toward H8. The OLMo rerun of both tasks on the same papers (tools/code_papers_open.py) is the planned cross-model check.

gates.advance: g24 gate() on the advance codings of the full-run tag (the 40 human-rated gold papers are in it); until it passes, outcomes are reported as the model judgment of reported warrant
gates.disclosure: g30 on round 2 (tag r2-review-v2) against g27 labels of round 2, restricted to the kinds tried_dropped and added_for_review (g30 --kinds, output derived/translation/disclosure_agreement_r2_oo.json): final-status alpha (nominal) >= 0.667 on matched items and detection precision >= 0.6. Round 2 because the instrument was developed on round 1. g27 is one agent labeller of the same model family, not a reference standard
gates.absent_audit: human audit of 50 disclosures of kind tried_dropped or added_for_review with final_paper_status absent, drawn at random from the kept disclosures of the complete papers (C0-C4), stratified by set in proportion to their absent items (audit-sample, seed 2034); raters search the published XML text for the content; the gate passes when at least 80% are confirmed absent. Until both disclosure gates pass, outside-only features are reported as unvalidated model coding
gates.node_loop: node and loop of disclosures have no check; S4 uses loop and is reported only

power.note: power of the planned test (partial Spearman within journal x set strata, journals under MIN_STRATUM pooled within their set, Freedman-Lane permutation) on synthetic data: feature distribution of g27 round 1 (tried_dropped or added_for_review, final absent), achieved rate and score distribution of advance pilot 1, covariates independent of the feature, journal mix of the sets in each scenario (rounds 1 and 2 only for rounds_1_2). alpha 0.1 is the BH threshold when most of the family is non-null; alpha 0.1/8 when H1 is the only non-null hypothesis (BH rank 1).
